algorithm: a. Find opening brace '{' at position pos
b. Track depth, inString, stringChar, escape through all characters
c. Brackets inside string values ({, }, [, ]) do NOT affect depth tracking
d. When depth returns to 0, extract the substring from '{' to matching '}'
e. Attempt JSON.parse() first; fall back to new Function() if JSON.parse fails
f. Only keep non-array objects that have a CorrectChoice field
g. Advance pos past the closing brace and continue
a. Read obj.CorrectChoice (direct property access from the SAME object)
b. If CC is not A/B/C/D → skip
c. Read obj['ExplanationWrong' + CC] (direct property access, same object)
d. If value is non-empty string → flag as DL-008

verdict.statement: The upgraded governance guard Rule 2 (extractObjectsFromText + within-object property access) correctly handles all four DL-029 edge cases in this simulation: (1) realistic CC→EW distances exceeding the old 1200-char window, (2) adjacent objects with cross-object CC contamination risk, (3) Pack B format with CC-before-QID field ordering, and (4) brackets inside string values. The old ±1200 window-scan approach produces 0 true positives, 2 false negatives, and 1 false positive on the same test content — a complete failure of detection. The new approach produces 2 true positives, 0 false negatives, and 0 false positives — perfect detection.
remainingRisks: The extractObjectsFromText approach uses JSON.parse() as primary parser with new Function() as fallback. If a file contains content that neither parser can handle (e.g., unescaped control characters in strings), objects will be silently skipped. This is the VM-004 scenario from the Parse Spec — objects are present but not parsed. The governance guard currently does not log a warning when this happens.

The approach requires the fragment to contain complete JSON objects (matching '{' and '}'). Edit fragments that contain partial objects (e.g., an edit that replaces only the ExplanationWrongB field value) will NOT produce any extracted objects → DL-008 check is silently skipped. The Parse Spec §6.1 addresses this: for edit operations, the governance guard should read the full file, apply the edit in-memory, and parse the complete result. This is NOT yet implemented in the current governance guard (the current code scans only newContent for edits).

The current governance guard (line 70) requires obj.CorrectChoice to be truthy for object inclusion. If an object has CorrectChoice = '' (empty string, which is falsy), it will be skipped entirely. This is the correct behavior since empty CC is invalid, but it means the guard would miss detecting DL-008 in an object where CC is somehow non-conforming.

recommendations: R1: Implement the Parse Spec §6.1 edit-operation handling — read full file from disk, apply edit in-memory, parse complete result. This closes the edit-fragment-blindness gap (VM-004).

R2: Add a warning log when extractObjectsFromText finds '{' start markers but produces fewer objects than expected (e.g., found 4 '{' but only 2 objects parsed). This would catch silent parse failures.

R3: Consider adding the AM-1 Function Constructor parse (parse whole array at once) as a verification pass on the full file post-edit, not just on the edit fragment. The extractObjectsFromText approach (AM-3) is correct for detecting DL-008 in edit fragments, but a full-file AM-1 parse on the post-edit file would catch any DL-008 violations introduced in other parts of the file by the edit's side effects.

R4: Update the test suite (test_governance_guard.js lines 356-367) — the existing DL-029 test uses compact fabricated objects where cross-object CC capture is trivially avoided. Add a test with realistic distances (>1500 chars CC→EW) to verify the object-boundary approach works on pack-file-realistic content.
